learningObjective: Create one mapped copy per original node, then reproduce every adjacency entry between copies.

mechanismReview.pattern: Breadth-first graph traversal plus an original-node to copied-node identity map.
mechanismReview.recognitionCue: A cyclic connected object must be deep-copied while preserving adjacency, so each original identity needs exactly one reusable copied identity before edges are wired.
mechanismReview.invariant: Every key in copies maps to exactly one clone, and after an original node is processed, its clone has one copied neighbor entry for every original neighbor processed in order.
mechanismReview.stateModel: Keep a queue of discovered originals and a map from each original object to its clone. The map doubles as the visited set and as the lookup used to build clone-to-clone edges.
mechanismReview.visualRationale: Showing original and copied nodes together with real edges, the queue, and the identity map makes cycles, reuse, and the prohibition on edges back to originals directly visible.
rejectedAlternatives: A node-value table cannot show whether copied adjacency points to originals or clones.
A recursive call tree duplicates shared graph nodes and misrepresents cyclic topology.
A final before-and-after snapshot hides when the map prevents duplicate copies.
mechanismReview.transferLesson: When copying any cyclic object graph, allocate and memoize an object before traversing its references, then resolve every copied reference through that memo.

mediumRationale: An original, problem-specific trace shows the actual input, changing state, safe transition, and result. The static first frame works without JavaScript; controls add step-by-step playback without replacing the proof with decoration.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: automatic graph layout would hide the exact data values and state changes that this problem needs.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: the trace is a changing data state, so semantic HTML keeps values selectable, readable, and responsive.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected: each problem owns concrete frames rendered as arrays, maps, grids, trees, stacks, queues, intervals, pointers, bits, or tensor shapes.
mediumComparison.interaction: Selected as progressive enhancement: Play, Previous, Next, and step buttons reveal the same authored frames while static HTML remains complete.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the visual is an original synthesis of the supplied implementation and does not reuse source artwork.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose alone would make the learner simulate the changing data structure in working memory.

deckReview.notes: No source slide deck is part of the supplied coding guide. The visual was designed from this problem's source implementation and worked trace.

sourceReview.notes: The supplied Coding_Questions_Phone_Guide.md is the curriculum source. The task, implementation sketch, and complexity statement are preserved; the trace frames are original explanatory artwork.
